newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germans should cut overtime to create jobs - Jagoda.
newsitem.headline: Germans should cut overtime to create jobs - Jagoda.

text.p: Germans should work fewer overtime hours in the interest of creating new jobs, Federal Labour Office President Bernhard Jagoda said on Friday.
A record two billion hours of overtime was posted in 1996. "That was much too much," Jagoda said in an interview with the Stuttgarter Nachrichten newspaper.
High unemployment, which hovered round the post-unification record of four million throughout 1996, remains Germany's most pressing political problem.
Ursula Engelen-Kefer, vice-chairman of the DGB trade unions association, said 370,000 jobs could be created if the record level of overtime were reduced by 40 percent.

"Converting overtime to jobs wouldn't cost employers more money," Engelen-Kefer said in a radio interview. She still thinks it possible to meet the goal of halving German unemployment by the year 2000.

Jagoda added that too many jobs, particularly in the commercial sector, were performed by workers who earned less than 590 marks a month, the minimum for paying social security fees. This strains the social security system, he said.
"If the new shop opening hours law leads only to the creation of more 590-mark jobs, that is a big mistake," he said.
Germany recently changed its laws to allow shops to stay open longer, but most retailers are spreading their workforces thinner rather than taking on new workers.
Employers should make more use of part-time workers who can work flexible hours, Jagoda said.
